investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state and the agent was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining VM slots (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining VM slots (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-06 with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0/6 nodes could schedule the eval pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a Kubernetes cluster resource constraint, not a confirmed user-facing product outage.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent eval pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (0 allocatable VM slots remaining), and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector requirements. Preemption was also unavailable on all 6 nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 145 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and a full contract gap across all 5 required fields. The same scheduling failure independently blocked remote-agent-create (128 s) and remote-agent-state (147 s), confirming the constraint is at the cluster/node-pool layer shared by all remote-agent eval pods, not in the eval runner logic or the application API itself.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots on the kata/peerpods-capable nodes are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the eval pod's scheduling constraints restrict it to nodes that support kata peer-pods isolation, and 4 nodes in the cluster do not carry the required label or taint, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are also at capacity, the pod is guaranteed to be Unschedulable.

TERTIARY — transient burst of concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all VM slots simultaneously: if other scheduled jobs, user-initiated remote agents, or parallel eval runs were active at the same time, they could have temporarily exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota. The three sibling checks failing sequentially over ~5 minutes suggests the exhaustion was sustained, not a brief spike.

LOW PROBABILITY — node pool scaling lag: the cluster autoscaler may not have added new kata-capable nodes quickly enough to absorb the eval pod demand, or autoscaling is not configured for the kata node pool.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence fields with the message containing 'hello from aura', the scheduling constraint has resolved and the failure was transient capacity exhaustion rather than a persistent misconfiguration.

If kubectl describe nodes shows that the 2 kata-capable nodes have available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and the pod still fails to schedule, the root cause is the node affinity/selector mismatch rather than VM slot exhaustion.
If the node affinity/selector on the eval pod matches nodes that do not carry kata.peerpods.io/vm at all, the scheduling failure is a pod spec misconfiguration rather than a capacity problem.

If only remote-agent-runtime fails while remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state pass in a subsequent run, the failure is isolated to the runtime probe's pod spec or timing rather than a shared cluster-level constraint.
If the local-agent-runtime eval (which shares the same evidence contract shape) also fails with a scheduling error, the problem may extend beyond the remote kata node pool to a broader cluster issue.

Add a pre-scheduling readiness check for the remote-agents feature that verifies at least one kata-capable node has available VM slots, allowing the eval suite to skip or warn rather than time out when capacity is known to be zero.

Add a node affinity/selector validation eval that confirms the expected number of nodes match the remote-agent pod's scheduling constraints, catching misconfigurations before they cause scheduling failures.

Consider a canary eval that attempts remote-agent pod scheduling with a minimal resource request and no workload, purely to validate scheduler reachability and VM slot availability as a leading indicator.
